# discord_application_command (Resource)

Manages a global Discord application command (slash, user, or message command).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "discord_application_command" "ping" {
  application_id = "123456789012345678"
  name           = "ping"
  description     = "Replies with pong"
  type           = 1 # CHAT_INPUT (slash command)

  # Options are JSON to support arbitrarily nested subcommands and groups.
  options = jsonencode([
    {
      type        = 3 # STRING
      name        = "message"
      description = "Optional message to echo"
      required    = false
    },
  ])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `application_id` (String) Snowflake ID of the application. Changing this forces a new command.
- `name` (String) Command name (1-32 characters).

### Optional

- `default_member_permissions` (Set of String) Permission names a member needs by default to use the command. Empty/unset means everyone.
- `description` (String) Command description (required for CHAT_INPUT/slash commands, 1-100 characters).
- `dm_permission` (Boolean) Whether the command is available in DMs with the app (global commands only).
- `nsfw` (Boolean) Whether the command is age-restricted.
- `options` (String) Command options as a JSON array. Carried as JSON to support arbitrarily nested subcommands and groups. Compared semantically, so formatting differences do not cause drift.
- `type` (Number) Command type: 1 CHAT_INPUT (default), 2 USER, 3 MESSAGE. Changing forces a new command.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The command snowflake ID.
- `version` (String) Autoincrementing version identifier updated on each command change.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Global commands are imported using "application_id:command_id".
terraform import discord_application_command.ping 123456789012345678:987654321098765432
```
